questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my German, and widen the academic options for my last semester at the Master. Berlin has far more available courses, and cultural offers, compared to Copenhagen

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am really happy that I went even though the workload is remarkably higher, it has given me many new experiences.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information is a little hidden at FU, but I have been on exchange priorly and knew where to look.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is a really good Erasmus- and Exchange office ready to help at campus as well as over email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think it would be harder if I didn't know where to look, who to ask, and it really helps knowing that the system is very flexible and wants to help you get through the administrative tasks.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is very difficult, I looked at facebook groups, old contacts and WG-websites and ended up connecting with someone who had a room free.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is really nice living a bit closer to the city, but I would recommend looking at the public transport connections. From my first room I had an hour to campus, from the second only a half - I felt it made a difference, also allowing me to bike.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't use the housing for students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are many things to remember and many deadlines to meet - but in the end they want you to come and will do a lot to help, so that felt very safe.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied through my home-university. The hardest is the OLA and the pre-approval, since the courses aren't available when you're applying, so you have to apply with old courses and then get the changes accepted whilst on exchange.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had both my sending Erasmus office and my receiving, so I felt very helped. Other than this there are also a lot of information online and documents that guide through the different portals. The best help is not to stress, since it will all be fine at the end.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the courses i wanted, both by writing the professors and through application letters.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it! Don't stress, and reach out when you're confused: The portals are many and the requirements seem overwhelming, but they will help you if you write or seek out a counselling sessions and the professors are happy to make individual adjustments most of the time. And maybe remember that there has for sure been someone before forgetting a deadline or having to re-send information to get everything approved, so there are no stupid questions or mistakes and there are admin offices on both ends ready to ask for what they need in order to confirm your stay.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I like that I can choose completely freely.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were notably higher than those I took on my BA, and since you have quite many to meet the 30 ECTS it is a little stressful to keep up.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had more different classes and different professors. They all do it differently: For one they check participation and will often check that you read through pre-class reflections fx - and you can only miss two classes. I didn't like this lack of trust in me as a student, and it made it a bit overwhelming to then juggle four different classes at the same time, but I am happy about the level and the amount I learned through this extra push.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
32114 Queer Art: New Critical Readings from the Americas  
13501 Theories and Methods in Modern Art 
17390 Ü-Literary and Cultural Theories: Reading the Past: 
Historicism, Presentism, Hauntology 
16583 The Aesthetics and the Politics of Collapse

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The courses aren't repeated but I would really recommend Sabine Schülting - she's a GREAT prof!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I travelled to see my girlfriend (those are the other fees)
The local transport is included in the Semester Fee you pay at the beginning and the all public is open to you. I bought a bike as well for 150EURO.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I wasn't surprised: The food had gotten a little more expensive - both in the supermarket and eating out, but it is the same all over. 
I put my budget pretty high in order to also enjoy being in a new city and trying out what it could offer.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I went to multiple sports-courses, they are great ways to feel attachment to the city and find cute people to hang out with.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I went to the uni-sport, there are also Erasmus-excursions, though I didn't get to try them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Spooorts! I went to both tango and balfolk and joined the social-dancing events as well.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would go to the lakes for sure, they are nice small escapes, and to Leipzig that aren't too far away. Other than that I would keep an eye on ICI, that has great talks, and the theatres. Also the clubs are worth visiting and many of the museums - fx Hamburger Bahnhof and Körnerpark Galerie.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy, the german culture isn't too far from the danish, and in Berlin there are also many different and international people, so you'll fit right in.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would ask people in my course for a coffee, join sports and events also with Erasmus-students fx from a language course. Other than that dating and friendsdating are sweet ways to encounter new people, and you literally have almost nothing to lose, since every new person is a potential contact.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't encounter any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really like the layed-back-ness of Berlin, the no rush and everything can take a little longer!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember that all admin will end up working out - also the ones you can't solve immediately
Berlin is lovely, so go out explore, and it's a great city to hang out alone in - they all do it:-)
If it all get's a little much, then Krumme Lanke can give you some breathing space, it's the end of the train ride to uni anyways.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the professors and don't be shy about taking courses outside your institute.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to find an everyday in another city and feeling like I grew an extra home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The admin hanging a little over your head, since it can sometimes be hard to relax when everything feels a little out of control.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
